text:
Good evening. The cold front is sliding through right now, and the clouds and the odd sprinkle should be done by about 5. Sunset is at 5:50, and I wouldn't count on a big show, though the sky should clear out after dark. Today ended near 55, but that's the last of the mild air. It turns breezy from about 7 to 10 tonight as the cold air pours in, then the wind settles. We bottom out around 33, with some spots dipping into the upper 20s, so a little frost on the windshield is likely in the morning.

Tuesday is sunny but a good eight or nine degrees cooler, with a high near 46 and only a light breeze. Wear the real coat. Tuesday night is the coldest of the season so far, with a low around 26 under clear skies, so cover or bring in anything tender. Wednesday starts frosty, then climbs to the low to mid 50s.

Mostly sunny and a bit milder, with a high near 54 and a much less frigid night, low around 42.
Looks like a mostly sunny, mild day near 63, with showers likely holding off until evening and lingering into the night.
Showers may linger into early afternoon, then some sun, with a high near 61 and a cooler night.
Halloween looks mostly sunny and a touch cooler, with a high near 56, so trick-or-treating should stay dry and chilly.
Partly sunny and mild near 59 Sunday, with a few showers possible after midnight as clouds thicken.

  Tuesday Night: Mostly clear, with a low around 26. East wind 1 to 5 mph.
AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-26T18:44:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Behind a weak cold front this afternoon, high pressure will return with sharply colder air towards mid week.
  2. Light rain possible Thursday night as a frontal boundary moves through the region, then mostly dry and seasonably warm weather prevailing into the weekend.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 243 PM EDT Monday... No significant changes to the current forecast.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: GOES-19 visible satellite depicts a narrow moisture corridor associated with a weak cold front stretched across the region this afternoon. While most of the radar returns have ended up being virga, some locations in the St. Lawrence Valley have been able to pick up a few hundreths of an inch of rainfall. By and large however, many locations will remain dry with little to no measurable rain from this frontal system, especially those in Vermont where dewpoint depressions are 10-15 degrees. A few places along the northwest facing slopes of the Adirondacks and northern Greens, including Jay Peak, could a few sprinkles though due to orographic influences. Winds will turn to the north-northwest as the front moves through this afternoon advecting sharply colder air and some briefly gusty winds this evening from Canada. As nocturnal cooling begins after sunset this evening, winds will briefly increase in the northern Champlain Valley up to 25 MPH or so between 7-10 PM. Winds will weaken towards calm thereafter. Tonights lows will cool to the upper 20s for many locations with a few locations hovering around the freezing mark in the wider valleys; coldest locations will be across northern New York and the Northeast Kingdom. Tomorrow will feature sunny skies with continued cool high temperatures struggling to reach the upper 40s. The coldest night of the season arrives Tuesday night under strong radiational cooling. Overnight lows may approach some records for Montpelier and St. Johnsbury, with records elsewhere residing in the 10th percentile or lower. Temperatures will drop to the teens across the Adirondacks and low 20s elsewhere. Temperatures slowly rebound Wednesday as high pressure and south winds help to moderate our pattern. Temperatures will warm to the low to mid 50s. KEY MESSAGE 2: Low chances for some showers on Thursday night as a front crosses our area. With center of the low passing well north of our area, not a lot of strong forcing with this frontal passage. If we have precipitation, it will be light. Then we once again expect mostly dry and seasonably warm weather for Friday and Saturday as a ridge of surface high pressure builds into the north country. Some models indicate increasing chances for showers early next week, but not a lot of model consistency in that timeframe at this point. .

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Our stretch of beautiful bluebird skies has been interrupted with widespread overcast skies across Vermont and the North Country. A weak cold front is slipping south this evening with little more than a sprinkle north and a gusty northwesterly breeze to 25 mph in the Champlain Valley between 7 and 10 p.m. Tonight turns partly cloudy and chilly with lows near 29, then Tuesday high pressure brings the sunny skies back but with the coldest night of the season so far Tuesday night. Friday stays partly sunny and mild with highs near 62 and a 40 percent chance of scattered morning showers, then drying Friday night with lows near 39. Saturday (Halloween!) brings mostly sunny skies and highs near 57, followed by partly sunny and warmer weather Sunday into Monday with highs near 60 to 62.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-26T16:53:00Z — same caveat): Cloudy north, brighter and warmer south Monday afternoon — Expect a mostly cloudy sky with a few spot showers in northern areas Monday afternoon, due to a cold front on approach. Highs reach the upper 50s there. Southern Vermont looks brighter overall, where highs again push well into the 60s. The sky clears out tonight, but it turns colder and breezy. Temperatures fall back to the 20s and low 30s for most. Teens are possible in the Adirondacks. Tuesday will feature nearly full sunshine, but it will be unseasonably cool. Highs only reach the mid to upper 40s, with a noticeable north breeze. Wednesday starts with another widespread freeze, but it turns seasonable by afternoon, with highs in the mid-50s and a partly sunny sky. Another warmup arrives late week with highs approaching 70 on Thursday, thanks to a gusty south breeze. After a sunny start, clouds increase through the afternoon. Another cold front brings a few showers Thursday night, though not expecting significant rain. A couple showers linger Friday, otherwise expecting a nice day with a mix of sun and clouds. Highs will be near 60. Halloween weekend looks dry and seasonable, with partial sunshine and highs in the 50s to around 60.
